title: Stress-induced Antibiotic Susceptibility Testing on a Chip
protocol: Vigorously mix PDMS and curing agent in a 10:1 ratio.
Degas the viscous mixture in a vacuum chamber for 1 hour at room temperature.
Pour the PDMS slowly over the aluminum mold from the center.
Ensure to leave the pins uncovered while pouring.
Stop pouring once the target weight is achieved (4 g of PDMS and 0.4 g of curing reagent).
Level the mold inside an oven and cure at 37 °C overnight.
Alternatively, cure for 2 hours at 60 °C or 1 hour at 90 °C.
Dissect the cured PDMS layer along the edge of the mold.
Carefully peel off the cured PDMS layer with a pair of forceps.
Clean the mold surface with 70% ethanol and a Q-tip.
Place the glass window into the flow cell pocket.
Lay a coated glass slide over the glass window inside the pocket of the flow cell with the active side up.
Place the PDMS layer with channels facing down on top of the glass slide.
Align channel inputs with through-holes in the metal plate.
Gently push air out from between the layers.
Flip the PDMS/glass slide assembly so that the PDMS faces the glass window.
Overlap PDMS channel inputs with through-holes in the metal plate.
Place the pressure plate on top and tighten the screws.
Place the assembled flow cell under the microscope.
Set the microscope magnification to 60X.
Prealign the channel positions.
Inoculate 50 ml of Mueller Hinton broth containing 2% NaCl (MH2) with a bacterial colony.
Shake at 250 rpm overnight at 37 °C.
Mix 50 µl of overnight bacteria culture into 50 ml of MH2 media.
Shake at 250 rpm for 3 hr at 37 °C to ensure the bacteria are in log phase.
Thaw the fluorescent dye (5 mM stock) and lysostaphin (10 µg/ml stock) at room temperature.
Warm oxacillin powder to room temperature.
Take 10 ml of bacteria culture after the end of 3 hr subculture.
Centrifuge at 1,650 x g for 2 min.
Remove the supernatant from the bacteria.
Resuspend bacteria in 1 ml of fresh MH2 media.
Flush syringe tubing with 1 ml of media, leaving a little bit to avoid air bubbles.
Load 0.7 ml of bacteria type 1 into the syringe.
Fill two channels of the flow cell with bacteria type 1.
Watch for liquid appearance on the other side of the channel after approximately 150 µl is added.
Place the flow cell inside the incubator at 37 °C for 45 min to allow bacterial settling and attachment.
Prepare 140 µl of 0.5 mM fluorescent dye solution by mixing 14 µl of fluorescent dye stock with 126 µl of MH2 media.
Dilute 10 mg of oxacillin in 40 ml of MH2 media to obtain a final concentration of 250 µg/ml oxacillin.
Prepare 130 ml of control solution by mixing 65 µl of fluorescent dye, 9.12 µl of lysostaphin stock, and 130 ml of MH2 media.
Prepare 130 ml of antibiotic solution with final concentrations of 0.25 µM fluorescent dye.
Add 65 µl of fluorescent dye (0.5 mM) to the antibiotic solution.
Add 9.12 µl of lysostaphin stock (10 µg/ml) to the antibiotic solution.
Add 26 ml of oxacillin (250 µg/ml) to the antibiotic solution.
Add 104 ml of MH2 media to complete the preparation of the antibiotic solution.
Mix all components thoroughly in a container to ensure uniform distribution of reagents.
Fill two 60 ml syringes with control solution.
Fill two 60 ml syringes with prepared antibiotic solution.
Wrap solutions in aluminum foil to prevent light-induced degradation.
Overfill syringes to account for loss due to flushing of the tubing.
Remove air bubbles from the syringes by flicking.
Attach and fill input tubing to the tip with experimental solution.
Mount syringes onto the pump, placing the smallest volume syringe first.
Lock the plunger position on the first syringe after mounting.
Fit remaining syringes onto the pump, squeezing plungers as necessary.
Set the pump speed to 1 ml/min.
Set the pump volume to 60 ml.
Do a flush with the pump until a steady stream of liquid is seen from all syringes.
Remove flow cell from centrifuge and mount it onto microscope stage.
Connect input/output tubing to each of the flow cell channels (one input/one output per channel).
Collect output into four different containers for individual channel volume measurement.
Check prealigned positions from step 2.5.
Adjust settings if the field-of-view is not centered or out-of-focus, then save new positions.
Set phase contrast acquisition time to 10 msec and fluorescence acquisition time to 1600 msec.
Obtain phase contrast and fluorescence images for each position before initiating flow.
Start liquid flow and immediately check focus on the bottom of the channels.
Take phase contrast and fluorescence images within the first minute of flow.
Acquire images every 2 minutes after the initial set until 60 minutes of flow have occurred.
Refocus as necessary.
Make a 10% bleach solution in a beaker (100 ml).
Fill 4 x 20 ml syringes with 10 ml of the mixture and debubble them.
Attach syringes to the flow cell; process takes approximately 1-2 minutes for clearing bacteria.
Set pump speed to 1 ml/min and volume to 3 ml, run for 3 min.
Fill 4 x 60 ml syringes with DI water and debubble them.
Attach syringes to the flow cell.
Set pump speed to 1 ml/min and volume to 30 ml, run for 30 min.
Monitor channel cleaning under microscope.
Disassemble the flow cell.
Discard the used epoxy slide.
Soak the flow cell components in DI water for 20 min.
Air dry.
Count the number of bacteria in each image using CellProfiler.
Import Nf and Np for individual images into data analysis software.
Calculate the fraction of dead bacteria (Nf / Np) at t = T.
Subtract the fraction of dead bacteria present at the outset of the experiment from both control and experimental channels.
Subtract the fraction of dead bacteria in the control channel from that in the experimental channel at each time point.
Graph DPnorm vs. t for the course of the experiment.
